sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Relationships column: on an artist's releases, release groups and works, a label's releases, a release group's and a recording's releases, and an area's labels, the column now asks MusicBrainz's Web Service for up to 100 rows per request instead of one request per row — about 24 requests instead of 2 300 for a large discography, i.e. under a minute instead of about 42 minutes when the service is not busy. The bulk answers carry the same relationships as per-row lookups (checked on 51 entities across these 7 page types) and go into the same cache, so other pages listing the same entities get them for free. Rows a bulk answer does not contain, such as a Various Artists view, are still looked up one by one, and bulk fetching stops by itself as soon as one-by-one would be cheaper. The completion toast says how many rows came from bulk requests.
New setting 'Relationships: fetch whole pages at once where MusicBrainz allows it' (sa_rel_browse_batch_enable, default on) switches bulk fetching off.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Relationships column: every cell now shows a small, faint glyph saying where that row stands — 🔗 not loaded yet, ⋯ queued (the column is still fetching), ◌ loading, – loaded but nothing with an icon, ⚠ the request failed. In a huge table where only a few rows have relationships, you can now see at a glance which rows have been looked up and which are still waiting, without the debug console.

Relationships column: click a cell to load just that row — one request — even while the column is collapsed; the rest of the table stays collapsed and untouched. Clicking a queued row while the column is still fetching gets it ahead of the queue, and clicking a failed (⚠) row retries it. On a loaded cell, hovering shows ⟳: clicking the cell outside its icons re-fetches that row, bypassing the cache. Rows loaded by hand survive filtering, sorting and multi-table re-renders, and emptying the column (▼🔗) while a row is still loading discards its late answer.

New setting 'Relationships: show a load-state glyph in each cell' (sa_rel_cell_state_glyphs, default on) hides the glyphs and turns click-to-load off. The glyphs are drawn purely by CSS, so filters, sorting, the 📊 dropdown, exports and Save to Disk never see them.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Relationships column: the icon writer and the failure marker moved out of the column's fetch pass into shared module-level functions (_relWriteResult, _relWriteFailure, _relMasterCellsFor), so a bulk pass and a single-row load write cells through the same idempotent code.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Relationships column: a failed MusicBrainz Web Service request (an HTTP 503 while the service is shedding load, or a network error) was shown exactly like 'this release has no relationships', and stayed that way for the rest of the session because the failure was cached in memory. A failed request is now retried up to 3 times with a widening backoff and is never cached; the cell is marked failed rather than done; it is not re-requested on every filter keystroke; and it is retried when the column is collapsed and expanded again, or with the 🔗⟳ retry buttons. The completion toast and status bar say how many requests failed.

Relationships column: every request, including retries, now waits on one shared one-per-second rate limit, and a lookup already answered from the in-memory cache no longer waits a second before being shown. The millisecond Length batch source shares the same retry code, with unchanged behaviour.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Settings: the 'Enable Relationships column' description no longer claims the column applies only to four page types (artist-releasegroups, artist-releases, label-releases, releasegroup-releases) — it applies to every page type that declares it, including collections, series, tag pages, reports and search results — and now says what the icons come from (URL relationships of the row's release, release group, label or work, plus release/release-group relationships that have an icon).

Statistics panel: the 'Rel WS2 TTL evictions' row said cached relationship records expire after a '7-day TTL'; the default has been 30 days all along. It now shows the configured 'Relationships IDB cache TTL (days)' (sa_rel_idb_ttl_days) value.
